case_name: State Of Madhya Pradesh v Makhan @ Madan And Others
facts: On 15.7.1989 Premlal (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') had called a doctor for treatment of his sister and while he was returning after seeing off the doctor and reached near Kanji House Bazar Bohalla, accused persons had altercation with him and in order to kill, assaulted him by sticks and rod. They also threatened to set on fire his motorcycle at which Laxmi Bai and Maniya Bai (PW5) went there where they saw accused persons assaulting the deceased by rod and lathi as also by fists and slaps.

Thereafter the deceased was taken by his wife Somti Bai (PW1) and Maniya Bai (PW 5) to their house in unconscious condition. Report of the incident was given at 4.30 AM to the police station at Sarni, which is at a distance of about 9Km from the place of incident.
Premlal succumbed to his injuries on 20.7.1989. After his death, his dead body was sent for postmortem examination which was conducted by Dr. V.K. Shrivastava (PW 14).
The trial court as noted above found the accused persons guilty and convicted them. In appeal, however, the High Court directed the acquittal.
Since the accused persons pleaded innocence, the trial was held.

On 15.7.1989 Premlal had called a doctor for treatment of his sister and while he was returning after seeing off the doctor and reached near Kanji House Bazar Bohalla, accused persons had altercation with him and in order to kill, assaulted him by sticks and rod.
The deceased was shouting for help. Later he became unconscious and fell down and the accused persons fled away from the place of occurrence.
petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the High Court should not have discarded the evidence of the eye witnesses.
respondent_arguments: Learned counsel for the respondent on the other hand supported the judgment of the High Court.
court_reasoning: In view of what has been stated above, the judgment of the High Court does not suffer from any infirmity to warrant interference.
If that be so, the evidence of Somti Bai (PW1) Maniya Bai (PW5), that they had clearly identified the accused persons cannot be believed.

It is true that even in darkness known persons can be identified from the manner of speech, style of walking and several other peculiar features. But the evidence of PW 2 was to the effect that because of darkness none of the accused persons could be identified.
In the instant case not only there is discrepancy as regards the place of occurrence but also on several vital aspects like non-disclosure and non-possibility of identification.
